title: Russell: percepts are the one part of the physical world known otherwise than abstractly

statements.text: Physics, Russell held, is exceedingly abstract. The intrinsic quality of the physical world is unknown, so the gap between percepts and physics is a gap in what is known, not a known difference in quality. Percepts are the only part of the physical world known otherwise than abstractly, and the distinction between physical and mental is, philosophically, superficial.

sources.quote: Physics, in itself, is exceedingly abstract
The gulf between percepts and physics is not a gulf as regards intrinsic quality, for we know nothing of the intrinsic quality of the physical world
Percepts are the only part of the physical world that we know otherwise than abstractly.
physical and mental is superficial and unreal
